claims.text: Bitcoin miner turned AI cloud that runs its own Texas data centers.
It started buying NVIDIA GPUs for an AI cloud business in 2023 and later renamed itself IREN after its Nasdaq ticker.
IREN reported revenue of $707.0M for the year to June 2026, with $128.8M from AI cloud services and $578.2M from Bitcoin mining.
It posted a net loss of $702.6M, driven by $638.8M of impairments on mining hardware it is retiring.
Microsoft signed a five-year, $9.7B contract in November 2025 for GB300 capacity at Childress, and IREN delivered the first 50 MW phase, Horizon 1, in August 2026.
NVIDIA followed in May 2026 with a five-year, $3.4B managed cloud contract for about 60 MW at Childress and a warrant to invest up to $2.1B in IREN shares.
IREN signed another $2.8B of multi-year contracts with AI developers in July 2026 and a contract with an unnamed frontier AI lab in August.
Childress hosts liquid-cooled GB300 NVL72 halls for Microsoft and air-cooled Blackwell systems for NVIDIA.
NVIDIA rated Horizon 1 an Exemplar Cloud for GB300 NVL72 after its own validation testing.
IREN targets 480 MW of gross AI cloud capacity (300 MW of IT load) by the end of 2026 and 1.2 GW gross in 2027.
Its pipeline of more than 5 GW includes the 2 GW Sweetwater hub in Texas, where 300 MW is under construction for Q4 2027, plus sites in Oklahoma, Canada, Spain and Australia.
NVIDIA contract = $3.4B over 5 years (May 2026)
FY26 revenue = $707.0M, of which $128.8M from AI cloud
Capacity target = 480 MW gross in 2026, 1.2 GW in 2027
